Reason: The chest X-ray shows a well-defined cystic lesion in the right lower lobe traversed by a band-like opacity (indicated by arrows), which is characteristic of a dilated pulmonary vein crossing an intrapulmonary cyst. This anatomical relationship is clinically significant because interventions involving the cyst carry a risk of air embolism via this communicating vessel.
